commonPrompt: Create a genuinely NEW finished Kingdom Come painterly fantasy weapon illustration on TRANSPARENT background. One complete weapon only; no background, no environment, no pedestal, no text, border, shadow card, checkerboard or matte. Match the approved proof references' rich physical craftsmanship, attractive proportions, visible solid materials and restrained enchantment. The weapon must remain impressive if its small magical effect is mentally removed. Neutral reflected ivory-white illumination reveals steel/silver/bronze/obsidian/leather/bone planes; painterly game loot, NOT museum photography or plain generic historical equipment. Material construction is the primary attraction. Cultural motifs and forging matter more than region color. No rainbow, no prismatic treatment, no fully illuminated blade, no lightning outlines, no bright particle cloud, no giant colored energy channels. Except where explicitly requested, magic remains in a few small inscriptions, core or seal without an outer glow. An explicitly requested SLIGHT glow is confined immediately to its small magical component, never the entire weapon. Keep its full silhouette, every tip and pommel inside the square canvas; leave transparent clearance so nothing is clipped. New original geometry, not a recolor or reused reference body. Crisp recognizable physical silhouette at 60px and 76px. Preserve painterly detail and natural materials.

remainingTwelve.name: Marchwatch Spear
remainingTwelve.brief: A distinctive mountain-forged fantasy spear with a broad steel leaf point clasped between two unequal wing-shaped dark-iron retainers, one short backward barb and a carved bone collar. Solid faceted steel, finely etched mountain knots, dark ashwood shaft and braided leather grip, compact ivory ferrule at the butt. A small translucent pale quartz piece is embedded in the neck with only a subtle cool glint. Neutral reflected light shows all metal planes. No glowing edge, no lightning, no crystalline neon blade. Attractive uncommon level15 craftsmanship; visibly simpler than elite arms.

remainingTwelve.name: Fenwarden Billhook
remainingTwelve.brief: An eerie elegant BILLHOOK with a broad inward-hooked tarnished-silver blade and an open teardrop gap held by rootlike ancient-metal ribs. Refined curving blade, solid metal flats, delicate flowing fen engravings, greenish aged patina and a restrained jade cabochon near the inner throat. Handle and ferrule have beautiful organic silver lattice around dark wood and leather. A faint teal rune at the throat is the only magical accent; it does not illuminate the entire blade or shaft. Unmistakable hooked silhouette, visible metal even without magic.

remainingTwelve.name: Sunscar Maul
remainingTwelve.brief: A prestigious compact desert maul with an angular stepped copper/bronze head and two clearly visible dark-steel striking faces. Rich geometric solar relief, actual layered construction, tiny engraved rivets and alternating polished/dark planes. The two cheeks lock around a SMALL faceted amber stone inside a protected recess, rather than a white-hot furnace occupying the head. Amber has a quiet inner warmth. Dark leather grip with copper rings and a small blocky counterweight. Solid mass, elegant dangerous proportions; never solid gold, never all glowing.

remainingTwelve.name: Frontier Falchion
remainingTwelve.brief: A beautifully forged dark-steel fantasy falchion with a deep curved belly, flared hooked point and three overlapping scale-like reinforcement plates on its spine. Broad solid blade surfaces reveal tempering patterns under neutral reflected highlights; a clean silver cutting bevel remains non-emissive. Unequal black-iron battlement quillons, fine bronze fasteners, oxblood leather grip and one small coal-red seal inside the guard. This seal has a barely perceptible ember glint, not molten cracks along the weapon. War-scarred but prestigious and sculptural.

remainingTwelve.name: Crownlands War Staff
remainingTwelve.brief: An imposing royal battle staff with a seven-sided silver lantern-crown head: three architectural heraldic ribs clasp an opaque ivory-enamel center with a small royal seal. Deep blue enamel bands and fine silver laurel relief are NON-luminous ornament. Long dark-steel shaft, graceful widely spaced silver collars and a pointed armored butt. Head broad enough to read at thumbnail size, excellent sculptural metalwork. A tiny pale rune is softly lit inside the crown, with no bright sapphire orb, no blue outline and no broad aura. Cultural prestige comes from construction and heraldry.

remainingTwelve.name: Blacksteel Warblade
remainingTwelve.brief: An aggressive masterwork broad seax-like warblade with a stepped forward point, thick bowed spine and two triangular structural cutouts near its base. Layered blackened steel, carefully polished neutral cutting facets and a recessed copper forge-ribbon make the metal beautiful and readable. A heavy asymmetrical broken-crown guard protects a textured black leather grip. One tiny recessed dark-crimson inscription is faintly enchanted inside the guard; the blade itself is solid, non-glowing and reflective. Avoid ember cracks running through every surface or full luminous outlines.

remainingTwelve.name: Highland Claymore
remainingTwelve.brief: An elite northern two-handed claymore with a broad leaf-shaped diamond-section steel blade, down-angled rugged crossguard ending in small OPEN RING terminals, and a long brown braided-leather grip with a plain octagonal iron pommel. Engraved mountain-knot bands, precise silver/iron contrasts and polished central facets make prestigious physical craftsmanship. A pair of small frost-white rune inlays near the ricasso has a faint internal shimmer only. No long crystal column, no glowing edge, no crescent/S-laurel guard. Must look fundamentally different from the royal solid parallel-sided Order Marshal Greatsword reference: rugged leaf silhouette, ring quillons, leather/iron construction.

remainingTwelve.name: Marshguard Glaive
remainingTwelve.brief: An elegant but unsettling ancient fen glaive with a tall sweeping crescent blade and a separate small hooked root-spur forming an open eye at its base. Solid tarnished silver blade, scalloped inner edge, beautiful flowing rootlike reinforcement and jade-green patina on engraved NON-luminous metal. A dark-wood shaft with silver vine collars and leather wrapping. A short enchanted inscription along only a small section of the inner blade produces a faint spectral teal shimmer; no full green outline, no giant orb and no fog cloud. More elaborate physical lattice than the lower billhook, but a clearly different ascending blade silhouette.

remainingTwelve.name: Crown Captain’s Halberd
remainingTwelve.brief: A regal silver-and-black halberd with a broad banner-shaped axe wing, tall three-faceted spear and a compact forked beak. A royal shield RELIEF at the junction is sculpted solid silver, with finely engraved laurel, dark-blue enamel, pale gilt fasteners and visible steel faces. Long square dark shaft, articulated silver collars, excellent balanced proportions. A tiny pair of platinum-white enchanted heraldic glyphs is recessed under the axe wing. No large blue gem, no bright-blue energy channel, no external aura. Regional identity from disciplined heraldic construction, not a color filter.

remainingTwelve.name: Mountain Warden’s Zweihander
remainingTwelve.brief: A massive northern fantasy zweihander with an ASYMMETRIC WAVY FLAMBERGE steel blade, long unsharpened ricasso, two blocky forward parrying lugs and a STRAIGHT block-ended iron crossbar. Long black two-handed grip and octagonal iron pommel. Three broad S-shaped waves create an unforgettable metal silhouette, clearly different from a leaf-shaped Highland Claymore or laurel-guard royal greatsword. A SMALL translucent glacial cylinder is pinned across the ricasso. Most blade surfaces remain solid steel with high-quality neutral reflected light and frozen engravings. Add only a SLIGHT localized ice-white/very pale-blue glow immediately around this small cylinder and adjacent few inches of blade. No lightning, full glowing edge, snow cloud or giant crystal blade.
remainingTwelve.magicTreatment: small glacial core with slight local glow

remainingTwelve.name: Frontier Marshal’s Poleaxe
remainingTwelve.brief: A prestigious battle-scarred poleaxe with three articulated black-iron hooked blade plates, a short angular rear pick and a tall diamond spear. Substantial visible steel faces and polished bevels, precise bronze pins and an armored dark shaft. Asymmetrical head and meaningful gaps between plates show advanced forging. One small deep-red furnace seal sits inside the head junction, quietly luminous within the metalwork; no external halo, no heated cutting outline or lava cracks throughout. Craftsmanship, mechanical layering and war-torn silhouette carry the prestige.

remainingTwelve.name: Imperial Thronehammer
remainingTwelve.brief: An endgame imperial polehammer with a huge stepped TRIANGULAR anvil head, a broad opaque faceted dark-steel striking face with obsidian inlays and a long downward-swept needle pick at the rear. Ancient imperial relief and dark-silver buttresses around two narrow protected windows, not a floating crystal head. Thick tapering armored shaft and architectural counterweight, no repeated gems on the shaft. Generous neutral reflected highlights make black steel/obsidian/silver materials visible. A concentrated small violet core shines only within the two head windows with a SLIGHT soft local glow just beside them. No purple lightning, outer blade contour, particle cloud or illuminated entire weapon. Must be distinct from the crescent-and-rectangular Gatehammer reference.
remainingTwelve.magicTreatment: protected violet windows with slight local glow

background: A single mechanically extracted actual-live-atlas background, not a newly generated backdrop. All illustrated foregrounds are genuinely image-generated.
